sections.markdown:
## When to recognize this pattern
Look for two coordinated indices over one search space, repeated work, or a prompt whose constraints rule out a quadratic scan.

## Core idea
Two pointers may converge from both ends of sorted data or move slow/fast in one direction. They can also perform an in-place partition or compaction. Correctness depends on proving which candidates can be discarded after each comparison. The template is a loop with an invariant, not simply two index variables.

```text
[1, 2, 4, 7, 11]
 L           R    sum too high -> R moves left
 L        R       sum too low  -> L moves right
```

sections.markdown:
## Naive approach
Start with all-pairs nested loops. It may be easy to verify, but it repeats work and becomes too slow as input grows. State its cost before optimizing.

## Better approach
Use left pointer/right pointer convergence and slow fast scans. The optimization is valid only if the invariant proves discarded work cannot affect the answer. Never quote a complexity without identifying the operation that dominates it.

## Time complexity
O(n) time after sorting. Explain whether sorting or preprocessing is included.

## Space complexity
O(1) auxiliary space. Input storage does not count as auxiliary space unless copied.

## Common mistakes
Using the pattern without its precondition, moving state in the wrong order, missing empty input, mishandling duplicates, and reporting average-case cost as a guarantee. For recursion, include call-stack space; for a DP table or hash map, count stored states.
